en: One cubic centimeter of solid gold weighs 19.3 grams, which is 19.3 times heavier than the exact same volume of liquid water.
When liquid water boils into steam, one milliliter of water expands to fill about 1,700 milliliters of space as a gas.
At room temperature, you can dissolve up to 204 grams of solid sugar into 100 milliliters of liquid water before the solution becomes saturated.
When iron undergoes a chemical change to form rust, it can expand up to three times its original volume and crumble.
Solid ice melts at 0 degrees Celsius, but solid tungsten metal requires a much hotter 3,422 degrees Celsius to melt.
A single water molecule is about 0.3 nanometers wide, making it roughly 300,000 times smaller than the width of a human hair.
In muddy water, suspended dirt particles are larger than 1,000 nanometers, while dissolved salt particles in saltwater are smaller than 1 nanometer.
A standard 12-inch helium balloon can lift about 14 grams, which is roughly the exact weight of two Philippine five-peso coins.
The Sun's surface is made of plasma at 5,500 degrees Celsius, which is 55 times hotter than boiling water's 100 degrees Celsius.
Mixing one teaspoon of baking soda with vinegar produces a chemical change that releases over 1,000 milliliters of carbon dioxide gas.
On the Mohs hardness scale, a diamond scores a perfect 10, while the softest mineral, talc, scores a 1.
In milk, fat droplets are between 100 and 1,000 nanometers wide, making them larger than dissolved sugar but too small to settle.
